speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with postpartum fever and abdominal tenderness; can you tell me how many days postpartum you are and what your fever temperature has been?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Postpartum endometritis. The patient's presentation of fever, abdominal/uterine tenderness, and increased urinary frequency following a prolonged labor is highly suggestive of intra-amniotic infection, which can lead to endometritis. The decreased bowel sounds may indicate early signs of peritonitis or ileus secondary to the infection.
